units.zh: 梁書卷第三十二 列傳第二十六
units.en: Book of Liang, Volume 32, Biography 26
units.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 32, Biographies 26

units.zh: 陳慶之 蘭欽
units.en: Chen Qingzhi; Lan Qin
units.literal: Chen Qingzhi; Lan Qin

units.zh: 陳慶之字子雲，義興國山人也。
units.en: Chen Qingzhi, styled Ziyun, came from Guoshan in Yixing commandery.
units.literal: Chen Qingzhi, styled Ziyun, was a native of Guoshan in Yixing.

units.zh: 幼而隨從高祖。
units.en: From childhood he attended Emperor Wu.
units.literal: In his youth he followed and attended the High Ancestor.

units.zh: 高祖性好棊，每從夜達旦不輟，等輩皆倦寐，惟慶之不寢，聞呼卽至，甚見親賞。
units.en: Emperor Wu loved weiqi and often played from dusk until dawn. His attendants all fell asleep from exhaustion, but Qingzhi alone stayed awake and answered every summons—behind this lay deep personal regard.
units.literal: The High Ancestor loved weiqi; he would play from night until dawn without stopping, and his companions all grew weary and slept, but only Qingzhi did not sleep; at a call he would arrive at once, and was greatly favored and prized.

units.zh: 從高祖東下平建鄴，稍爲主書，散財聚士，常思效用。
units.en: When Emperor Wu marched east to take Jianye, Qingzhi followed. He rose to chief secretary, spent his fortune gathering followers, and always looked for a chance to prove himself.
units.literal: Following the High Ancestor east to pacify Jianye, he gradually became Chief Secretary, dispersed his wealth to gather gentlemen, and constantly thought of rendering service.

units.zh: 除奉朝請。
units.en: He was made a palace attendant.
units.literal: He was appointed Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 普通中，魏徐州刺史元法僧于彭城求入內附，以慶之爲武威將軍，與胡龍牙、成景儁率諸軍應接。
units.en: During the Putong reign, Yuan Faseng, the Wei inspector of Xu province, asked at Pengcheng to defect to Liang. Qingzhi was named General of Martial Prestige and, with Hu Longya and Cheng Jingjun, led troops to take him in.
units.literal: In the Putong era, Yuan Faseng, Inspector of Xu province under Wei, at Pengcheng sought to enter and submit to the court; Qingzhi was made General of Martial Prestige and, with Hu Longya and Cheng Jingjun, led the armies to meet and receive him.

units.zh: 還，除宣猛將軍、文德主帥，仍率軍二千，送豫章王綜入鎮徐州。
units.en: After returning he was made General of Manifest Valor and commander of the Civil Virtue corps, and again led two thousand men to install Prince Zong of Yuzhang as garrison commander at Xu province.
units.literal: On his return he was appointed General of Manifest Valor and Commander of Civil Virtue, and still led two thousand troops to escort Prince Zong of Yuzhang to take up garrison at Xu province.

units.zh: 魏遣安豊王元延明、臨淮王元彧率衆二萬來拒，屯據陟□。
units.en: Wei sent Prince Yanming of Anfeng and Prince Yu of Linhuai with twenty thousand men to block them, encamping at a place whose name in the text is partly lost (Zhi□).
units.literal: Wei sent Prince Yanming of Anfeng, Yuan Yanming, and Prince Yu of Linhuai, Yuan Yu, with twenty thousand men to resist, encamped and holding [a place at] Zhi□.

units.zh: 延明先遣其別將丘大千築壘潯梁，觀兵近境。
units.en: Yanming first sent his lieutenant Qiu Daqian to fortify Xunliang and watch the Liang forces along the frontier.
units.literal: Yanming first sent his detached commander Qiu Daqian to build a stockade at Xunliang and observe the army near the border.

units.zh: 慶之進薄其壘，一鼓便潰。
units.en: Qingzhi pressed the stockade; a single charge broke it.
units.literal: Qingzhi advanced and pressed close to his stockade; at one drumbeat it collapsed.

units.zh: 後豫章王棄軍奔魏，衆皆潰散，諸將莫能制止。
units.en: Later Prince Zong of Yuzhang deserted to Wei. The army broke and fled, and no general could hold the men.
units.literal: Later the Prince of Yuzhang abandoned the army and fled to Wei; the masses all scattered in rout, and none of the generals could stop them.

units.zh: 慶之乃斬關夜退，軍士得全。
units.en: Qingzhi cut through the passes and withdrew by night, bringing the troops out intact.
units.literal: Qingzhi then cut through the passes and withdrew by night, and the soldiers were preserved whole.

units.zh: 普通七年，安西將軍元樹出征壽春，除慶之假節、總知軍事。
units.en: In the seventh year of Putong, General Yuan Shu of the west marched on Shouchun. Qingzhi received acting credentials and overall command of the campaign.
units.literal: In the seventh year of Putong, Anxi General Yuan Shu campaigned against Shouchun; Qingzhi was given acting credentials and overall command of military affairs.

units.zh: 魏豫州刺史李憲遣其子長鈞別築兩城相拒。
units.en: Li Xian, the Wei Inspector of Yu Province, sent his son Changjun to build two additional fortified towns in opposition.
units.literal: Li Xian, Inspector of Yu province under Wei, sent his son Changjun separately to build two cities to resist.

units.zh: 慶之攻之，憲力屈遂降，慶之入據其城。
units.en: Qingzhi attacked them. When Xian's strength gave out he surrendered, and Qingzhi occupied his towns.
units.literal: Qingzhi attacked them; Xian's strength was exhausted and he then surrendered, and Qingzhi entered and seized his cities.

units.zh: 轉東宮直閤，賜爵關中侯。
units.en: He was made a direct attendant in the Eastern Palace and enfeoffed as Marquis of Guanzhong.
units.literal: He was transferred to Direct Attendant of the Eastern Palace and enfeoffed as Marquis of Guanzhong.

units.zh: 大通元年，隸領軍曹仲宗伐渦陽。
units.en: In the first year of Datong he served under Commander-in-Chief Cao Zhongzong in the attack on Guoyang.
units.literal: In the first year of Datong, he was attached to the army of the Commander-in-Chief Cao Zhongzong in the campaign against Guoyang.

units.zh: 魏遣征南將軍常山王元昭等率馬步十五萬來援，前軍至駝澗，去渦陽四十里。
units.en: Wei sent General Who Conquers the South Prince Zhao of Changshan and others with a hundred and fifty thousand cavalry and infantry. The vanguard reached Tuojian, forty li from Guoyang.
units.literal: Wei sent the General Who Conquers the South, Prince Zhao of Changshan, Yuan Zhao, and others with one hundred fifty thousand horse and foot to relieve the city; the vanguard reached Tuojian, forty li from Guoyang.

units.zh: 慶之欲逆戰，韋放以賊之前鋒必是輕銳，與戰若捷，不足爲功，如其不利，沮我軍勢，兵法所謂以逸待勞，不如勿擊。
units.en: Qingzhi wanted to give battle. Wei Fang objected that the enemy vanguard would be picked troops: a victory would count for little, a defeat would sap the army's spirit. Better, as the strategists say, to let the weary come to you—do not engage.
units.literal: Qingzhi wished to meet them in battle; Wei Fang argued that the enemy vanguard must be light and elite troops—if battle went well it would not be enough for merit, and if it went badly it would damp our army's momentum; as the Art of War says, wait at ease for the weary—better not to strike.

units.zh: 慶之曰：「魏人遠來，皆已疲倦，去我旣遠，必不見疑，及其未集，須挫其氣，出其不意，必無不敗之理。
units.en: Qingzhi said, "The Wei troops have marched far and are already tired. They think we are still distant and will not expect a strike. Before they mass, we must break their spirit and hit them unawares—defeat is certain.
units.literal: Qingzhi said: "The Wei men have come from afar and are all already weary; they are already far from us and surely will not suspect us—before they have gathered, we must blunt their spirit and take them unawares; there is surely no principle by which we would not defeat them.

units.zh: 且聞虜所據營，林木甚盛，必不夜出。
units.en: Besides, their camp stands in thick woods—they will not march out at night.
units.literal: Moreover I hear that the camp the barbarians hold has very dense woods and they surely will not come out at night.

units.zh: 諸君若疑惑，慶之請獨取之。」
units.en: If you still doubt me, let me take them alone."
units.literal: If you gentlemen are in doubt, Qingzhi asks to take it alone."

units.zh: 於是與麾下二百騎奔擊，破其前軍，魏人震恐。
units.en: He then led two hundred horsemen in a headlong charge, routed the vanguard, and threw the Wei army into panic.
units.literal: Thereupon with two hundred horsemen under his command he charged in assault, broke their vanguard, and the Wei men were shaken with terror.

units.zh: 慶之乃還與諸將連營而進，據渦陽城，與魏軍相持。
units.en: Qingzhi rejoined the other commanders, advanced in linked camps, took Guoyang, and settled into a standoff with the Wei forces.
units.literal: Qingzhi then returned and, with the other generals linking camps, advanced and seized Guoyang city, and faced the Wei army in stalemate.

units.zh: 自春至冬，數十百戰，師老氣衰，魏之援兵復欲築壘於軍後，仲宗等恐腹背受敵，謀欲退師。
units.en: From spring through winter they fought scores of engagements until the army was worn down. Wei relief columns tried to build fortifications behind the Liang lines. Zhongzong and the others, fearing encirclement, planned to pull back.
units.literal: From spring to winter there were scores and hundreds of battles; the army grew old and its spirit waned. Wei's relief troops again wished to build stockades behind the army; Zhongzong and the others feared attack from front and rear and planned to withdraw the army.

units.zh: 慶之杖節軍門曰：「共來至此，涉歷一歲，糜費糧仗，其數極多。
units.en: Qingzhi stood at the camp gate with his staff of authority and said, "We have all been here a full year. The grain and arms we have spent are beyond counting.
units.literal: Qingzhi, staff of authority in hand at the army gate, said: "Together we have come to this place and passed a full year; grain and weapons wasted—the number is extremely great.

units.zh: 諸軍並無鬭心，皆謀退縮，豈是欲立功名，直聚爲抄暴耳。
units.en: The troops have no will to fight and only want to retreat. You did not come here for glory—you came to loot.
units.literal: The armies all have no fighting spirit and all plan to shrink back—how could this be wishing to establish merit and fame? You have simply gathered to plunder and ravage.

units.zh: 吾聞置兵死地，乃可求生，須虜大合，然後與戰。
units.en: They say armies on deadly ground fight to live. Wait until the enemy masses, then fight.
units.literal: I have heard that placing troops on deadly ground is how one may seek life; we must wait until the barbarians have gathered in full, and then give battle.

units.zh: 審欲班師，慶之別有密敕，今日犯者，便依明詔。」
units.en: If you mean to withdraw, I hold a secret order from the throne: anyone who retreats today dies by imperial command."
units.literal: If you truly wish to withdraw the army, Qingzhi has a separate secret edict: whoever offends today shall be dealt with according to the clear decree."

units.zh: 仲宗壯其計，乃從之。
units.en: Zhongzong was impressed and agreed.
units.literal: Zhongzong admired his plan and thereupon followed it.

units.zh: 魏人掎角作十三城，慶之銜枚夜出，陷其四壘，渦陽城主王緯乞降。
units.en: The Wei built thirteen linked strongpoints. Qingzhi led a silent night sortie, took four of them, and Guoyang's commander Wang Wei surrendered.
units.literal: The Wei men set up thirteen cities in pincer formation; Qingzhi went out at night with gags in the men's mouths, took four of their stockades, and Wang Wei, lord of Guoyang, begged to surrender.

units.zh: 所餘九城，兵甲猶盛，乃陳其俘馘，鼓噪而攻之，遂大奔潰，斬獲略盡，渦水咽流，降城中男女三萬餘口。
units.en: The other nine posts still held strong garrisons. He paraded prisoners and severed heads, stormed them with drum and shout, and drove them into rout. The slaughter filled the Guo River; more than thirty thousand men and women in the surrendered towns came over.
units.literal: Of the remaining nine cities the armor and weapons were still strong; he then displayed their captives and severed ears, attacked with drums and shouts, and they thereupon fled in great rout; those slain and captured were nearly all, the Guo River choked with the flow, and men and women of the surrendered cities numbered more than thirty thousand.

units.zh: 詔以渦陽之地置西徐州。
units.en: The court created Western Xu province on the Guoyang region.
units.literal: An edict established Western Xu province on the territory of Guoyang.

units.zh: 衆軍乘勝前頓城父。
units.en: The victorious army pushed on and encamped at Chengfu.
units.literal: The mass of armies, riding victory, advanced and encamped at Chengfu.

units.zh: 高祖嘉焉，賜慶之手詔曰：「本非將種，又非豪家，觖望風雲，以至於此。
units.en: Emperor Wu was delighted and sent Qingzhi a personal note: "You were born neither to a general's house nor to a great clan, yet you reached for wind and cloud and have come this far.
units.literal: The High Ancestor praised this and bestowed on Qingzhi a handwritten edict saying: "By origin you were not of a general's line, nor of a great house; you aspired to wind and cloud and have come to this.

units.zh: 可深思奇略，善克令終。
units.en: Think hard on bold strategy and see your career through to a worthy end.
units.literal: You may deeply ponder strange stratagems and well achieve a fine end.

units.zh: 開朱門而待賓，揚聲名於竹帛，豈非大丈夫哉！」
units.en: Open your gates to guests and let your name live in the histories—is that not the mark of a true man?"
units.literal: Open vermilion gates and await guests; raise your name on bamboo and silk—is this not a great man!"

units.zh: 大通初，魏北海王元顥以本朝大亂，自拔來降，求立爲魏主。
units.en: Early in Datong, Prince Hao of Beihai under Wei, citing turmoil at home, defected to Liang and asked to be set up as emperor of Wei.
units.literal: At the beginning of Datong, Yuan Hao, Prince of Beihai under Wei, because his own dynasty was in great disorder, came over of his own accord to surrender and asked to be established as ruler of Wei.

units.zh: 高祖納之，以慶之爲假節、飆勇將軍，送元顥還北。
units.en: Emperor Wu agreed and named Qingzhi acting-credentials holder and General of Swift Valor to escort Hao north.
units.literal: The High Ancestor accepted this and made Qingzhi acting-credentials holder and General of Swift Valor, to escort Yuan Hao back north.

units.zh: 顥于渙水卽魏帝號，授慶之使持節、鎮北將軍、護軍、前軍大都督，發自銍縣，進拔滎城，遂至睢陽。
units.en: At the Huan River, Hao took the Wei imperial title and gave Qingzhi full credentials as General Who Pacifies the North, army protector, and grand commander of the vanguard. They marched from Zhi county, took Yingcheng, and reached Suiyang.
units.literal: Hao at the Huan River assumed the title of Emperor of Wei and invested Qingzhi as bearer of credentials, General Who Pacifies the North, Protector of the Army, and Grand Commander of the Forward Army; setting out from Zhi county, he advanced and took Yingcheng, and then reached Suiyang.

units.zh: 魏將丘大千有衆七萬，分築九城以相拒。
units.en: The Wei commander Qiu Daqian had seventy thousand men and ringed the route with nine fortified towns.
units.literal: The Wei general Qiu Daqian had seventy thousand men and built nine cities in division to resist.

units.zh: 慶之攻之，自旦至申，陷其三壘，大千乃降。
units.en: Qingzhi attacked from dawn until mid-afternoon, took three strongpoints, and Daqian surrendered.
units.literal: Qingzhi attacked him; from dawn to the shen hour he took three stockades, and Daqian then surrendered.

units.zh: 時魏征東將軍濟陰王元暉業率羽林庶子二萬人來救梁、宋，進屯考城，城四面縈水，守備嚴固。
units.en: General Who Conquers the East Prince Yuye of Jiyin marched with twenty thousand imperial guards to relieve Liang and Song and encamped at Kaocheng, a town moated on every side and strongly held.
units.literal: At that time the Wei General Who Conquers the East, Prince Yuye of Jiyin, Yuan Yuye, led twenty thousand Forest Guard cadets to relieve Liang and Song, advanced and encamped at Kaocheng—the city on all four sides was girdled by water and its defenses were strict and solid.

units.zh: 慶之命浮水築壘，攻陷其城，生擒暉業，獲租車七千八百兩。
units.en: Qingzhi built floating stockades across the water, stormed the city, took Yuye alive, and seized seventy-eight hundred tax wagons.
units.literal: Qingzhi ordered floating works to build stockades on the water, attacked and took his city, captured Yuye alive, and obtained seven thousand eight hundred tax carts.

units.zh: 仍趨大梁，望旗歸款。
units.en: He pressed on to Daliang, where the defenders surrendered at sight of his banners.
units.literal: He then pressed on to Daliang; at sight of his banners they submitted.

units.zh: 顥進慶之衛將軍、徐州刺史、武都公。
units.en: Hao promoted him to General of the Guard, inspector of Xu province, and Duke of Wudu.
units.literal: Hao promoted Qingzhi to General of the Guard, Inspector of Xu province, and Duke of Wudu.

units.zh: 仍率衆而西。
units.en: The army marched west again.
units.literal: He still led the masses westward.

units.zh: 魏左僕射楊昱、西阿王元慶、撫軍將軍元顯恭率御仗羽林宗子庶子衆凡七萬，據滎陽拒顥。
units.en: Left Vice Director Yang Yu, Prince Qing of Xi'a, and Pacification Army General Yuan Xiangong led seventy thousand imperial guards and cadets to hold Yingyang against Hao.
units.literal: Yang Yu, Left Vice Director under Wei, Prince Qing of Xi'a, Yuan Qing, and Pacification Army General Yuan Xiangong led the imperial guard Forest Guard cadets and sons of the clans, in all seventy thousand, and held Yingyang to resist Hao.

units.zh: 兵旣精強，城又險固，慶之攻未能拔。
units.en: Their troops were elite and the city formidable; Qingzhi could not break it at first.
units.literal: The troops were already elite and strong, and the city was also perilous and solid; Qingzhi attacked but could not take it.

units.zh: 魏將元天穆大軍復將至，先遣其驃騎將軍尒朱吐沒兒領胡騎五千，騎將魯安領夏州步騎九千，援楊昱；
units.en: Yuan Tianmu's main army was closing in. He first sent Cavalry General Erzhu Tumener with five thousand barbarian horse and Cavalry Commander Lu An with nine thousand mixed troops from Xia province to reinforce Yang Yu;
units.literal: The Wei general Yuan Tianmu's great army was again about to arrive; he first sent his Cavalry General Erzhu Tumener with five thousand barbarian horsemen, and Cavalry Commander Lu An with nine thousand Xia province foot and horse, to relieve Yang Yu;

units.zh: 又遣右僕射尒朱世隆、西荊州刺史王羆騎一萬，據虎牢。
units.en: and Right Vice Director Erzhu Shilong and Western Jing inspector Wang Pi with ten thousand cavalry to hold Hulao.
units.literal: and also sent Right Vice Director Erzhu Shilong and Inspector of Western Jing Wang Pi with ten thousand horse to hold Hulao.

units.zh: 天穆、吐沒兒前後繼至，旗鼓相望。
units.en: Tianmu and Tumener arrived in succession until enemy banners filled the horizon.
units.literal: Tianmu and Tumener arrived one after another in succession; banners and drums faced one another.

units.zh: 時滎陽未拔，士衆皆恐，慶之乃解鞍秣馬，宣喻衆曰：「吾至此以來，屠城略地，實爲不少；
units.en: Yingyang still held, and the men were afraid. Qingzhi had the horses unsaddled and fed, then addressed the army: "Since we crossed the border we have sacked cities and seized land without number;
units.literal: At that time Yingyang was not yet taken and officers and masses were all afraid; Qingzhi then unslung his saddle and fed his horses, and announced to the masses: "From the time I came here until now, cities slaughtered and territory seized have truly been not a few;

units.zh: 君等殺人父兄，略人子女，又爲無算。
units.en: you have killed fathers and elder brothers and taken sons and daughters beyond counting.
units.literal: you gentlemen have killed men's fathers and elder brothers and seized men's sons and daughters—again beyond counting.

units.zh: 天穆之衆，並是仇讎。
units.en: Tianmu's host are nothing but blood enemies.
units.literal: Tianmu's masses are all blood enemies.

units.zh: 我等才有七千，虜衆三十餘萬，今日之事，義不圖存。
units.en: We are seven thousand against more than three hundred thousand. Today we fight with no thought of survival.
units.literal: We have only seven thousand; the barbarian masses are more than three hundred thousand—today's affair, by right we do not plan to survive.

units.zh: 吾以虜騎不可爭力平原，及未盡至前，須平其城壘，諸君無假狐疑，自貽屠膾。」
units.en: Their cavalry cannot match us on open ground, but not until they are all here. Take the city first. Do not hesitate and make yourselves meat for the pot."
units.literal: I hold that barbarian horse cannot contend for strength on the plain; before they have all arrived, we must level their city and stockades—you gentlemen must not borrow fox-like doubt and bring down slaughter and mince upon yourselves."

units.zh: 一鼓悉使登城，壯士東陽宋景休、義興魚天湣逾堞而入，遂克之。
units.en: At a single drumbeat he sent them up the walls. Song Jingxiu of Dongyang and Yu Tianmin of Yixing scrambled over the parapet and broke in; the city fell.
units.literal: At one drumbeat he had them all mount the wall; the stalwart Song Jingxiu of Dongyang and Yu Tianmin of Yixing crossed the parapet and entered, and thereupon took it.

units.zh: 俄而魏陣外合，慶之率騎三千背城逆戰，大破之，魯安於陣乞降，元天穆、尒朱吐沒兒單騎獲免。
units.en: Soon the Wei encirclement closed. Qingzhi led three thousand horse out from the city and shattered them. Lu An surrendered in the field; Tianmu and Tumener fled alone on horseback.
units.literal: Shortly the Wei battle lines closed from outside; Qingzhi led three thousand horse with the city at his back to meet them in battle and routed them greatly; Lu An begged to surrender on the field, and Yuan Tianmu and Erzhu Tumener escaped on single horses.

units.zh: 收滎陽儲實，牛馬穀帛不可勝計。
units.en: They seized Yingyang's stores—cattle, horses, grain, and silk beyond reckoning.
units.literal: They gathered Yingyang's stored goods; cattle, horses, grain, and silk could not be counted.

units.zh: 進赴虎牢，尒朱世隆棄城走。
units.en: They advanced on Hulao; Erzhu Shilong abandoned the town and fled.
units.literal: Advancing to Hulao, Erzhu Shilong abandoned the city and fled.

units.zh: 魏主元子攸懼，奔幷州。
units.en: The Wei emperor Yuan Ziyou fled in fear to Bing province.
units.literal: The Wei ruler Yuan Ziyou was afraid and fled to Bing province.

units.zh: 其臨淮王元彧、安豊王元延明率百僚，封府庫，備法駕，奉迎顥入洛陽宮，御前殿，改元大赦。
units.en: Prince Yu of Linhuai and Prince Yanming of Anfeng led the officials, sealed the treasuries, prepared the imperial train, and ushered Hao into the Luoyang palace. He took the throne hall, changed the reign title, and proclaimed a general amnesty.
units.literal: His Prince Yu of Linhuai, Yuan Yu, and Prince Yanming of Anfeng, Yuan Yanming, led the hundred officials, sealed the treasuries, prepared the imperial equipage, and welcomed Hao into the Luoyang palace; he took the front hall, changed the era name, and proclaimed a great amnesty.

units.zh: 顥以慶之爲侍中、車騎大將軍、左光祿大夫，增邑萬戶。
units.en: Hao made Qingzhi palace attendant, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and left grand master of splendid happiness, adding ten thousand households to his fief.
units.literal: Hao made Qingzhi Palace Attendant, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and increased his fief by ten thousand households.

units.zh: 魏大將軍上黨王元天穆、王老生、李叔仁又率衆四萬，攻陷大梁，分遣老生、費穆兵二萬，據虎牢，刁宣、刁雙入梁、宋，慶之隨方掩襲，並皆降款。
units.en: Grand General Prince Tianmu of Shangdang, Wang Laosheng, and Li Shuren marched again with forty thousand, took Daliang, and sent Laosheng and Fei Mu with twenty thousand to hold Hulao while Diao Xuan and Diao Shuang pushed into Liang and Song. Qingzhi ambushed them wherever they moved, and they all surrendered.
units.literal: The Wei Grand General Prince Tianmu of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, Wang Laosheng, and Li Shuren again led forty thousand men, attacked and took Daliang, and separately sent Laosheng and Fei Mu with twenty thousand troops to hold Hulao; Diao Xuan and Diao Shuang entered Liang and Song—Qingzhi struck by surprise wherever they went, and all submitted.

units.zh: 天穆與十餘騎北渡河。
units.en: Tianmu fled north across the river with only a dozen riders.
units.literal: Tianmu with a dozen or so horsemen crossed the river north.

units.zh: 高祖復賜手詔稱美焉。
units.en: Emperor Wu sent another personal note of praise.
units.literal: The High Ancestor again bestowed a handwritten edict praising him.

units.zh: 慶之麾下悉著白袍，所向披靡。
units.en: Qingzhi's men all wore white robes and swept aside everything before them.
units.literal: All under Qingzhi's command wore white robes; wherever they went, none could stand before them.

units.zh: 先是洛陽童謠曰：「名師大將莫自牢，千兵萬馬避白袍。」
units.en: A Luoyang children's rhyme had already run: "Famed commanders, do not think yourselves safe—thousands upon thousands flee the white robes."
units.literal: Earlier a children's rhyme in Luoyang said: "Famed generals and great commanders, do not hold yourselves secure—thousands of soldiers and ten thousands of horses avoid the white robes."

units.zh: 自發銍縣至於洛陽，十四旬平三十二城，四十七戰，所向無前。
units.en: From Zhi county to Luoyang, in a hundred and forty days he took thirty-two cities in forty-seven battles and met no equal.
units.literal: From setting out at Zhi county until Luoyang, in fourteen tens of days he pacified thirty-two cities and forty-seven battles—wherever he went, none stood before him.

units.zh: 初，元子攸止單騎奔走，宮衛嬪侍無改於常。
units.en: At first Ziyou had fled alone on horseback, yet the palace guards and consorts carried on as if nothing had changed.
units.literal: At first Yuan Ziyou fled on a single horse alone; palace guards and palace women attendants were unchanged from the usual.

units.zh: 顥旣得志，荒於酒色，乃日夜宴樂，不復視事。
units.en: Once Hao had his prize, he gave himself to wine and women, feasting day and night and neglecting government.
units.literal: Once Hao had achieved his aim, he was dissolute in wine and women; then day and night feasting and music, and he no longer attended to affairs.

units.zh: 與安豊、臨淮共立姦計，將背朝恩，絕賓貢之禮；
units.en: He and the princes of Anfeng and Linhuai plotted treachery, planning to turn on Liang and end the tribute owed the southern court;
units.literal: Together with Anfeng and Linhuai he set up a wicked plot, intending to turn against the court's grace and cut off the ritual of guest and tribute;

units.zh: 直以時事未安，且資慶之之力用，外同內異，言多忌刻。
units.en: but the realm was not yet secure, so for the moment they still needed Qingzhi's sword—outward allies, inward enemies, their speech sharp with suspicion.
units.literal: only because the times were not yet settled did they for the moment rely on Qingzhi's strength and use—outwardly the same, inwardly different, their words full of jealousy and harshness.

units.zh: 慶之心知之，亦密爲其計。
units.en: Qingzhi saw through them and laid plans of his own in secret.
units.literal: Qingzhi knew it in his heart and also secretly made plans of his own.

units.zh: 乃說顥曰：「今遠來至此，未伏尚多，若人知虛實，方更連兵，而安不忘危，須預爲其策。
units.en: He urged Hao, "We are far from home and many regions are not yet pacified. Once the enemy learns how few we are, they will mass again. In peace one must plan for danger.
units.literal: He then urged Hao: "Now having come from afar to this place, those not yet subdued are still many; if men know our emptiness and fullness, they will again link armies—in security do not forget peril; we must prepare plans in advance.

units.zh: 宜啓天子，更請精兵；
units.en: Ask the Son of Heaven for more elite troops;
units.literal: We ought to report to the Son of Heaven and request elite troops again;

units.zh: 並勒諸州，有南人沒此者，悉須部送。」
units.en: and order every province to send south all southerners held captive in the north."
units.literal: and also order the provinces that any southerners taken captive here must all be escorted and sent."

units.zh: 顥欲從之，元延明說顥曰：「陳慶之兵不出數千，已自難制；
units.en: Hao was inclined to agree, but Yuan Yanming warned him, "Chen Qingzhi commands only a few thousand men, and they are already hard to control.
units.literal: Hao wished to follow this; Yuan Yanming urged Hao: "Chen Qingzhi's troops do not exceed several thousand, and already by themselves are hard to control;

units.zh: 今增其衆，寧肯復爲用乎？
units.en: If you swell his ranks, will he still serve you?
units.literal: if we now increase his masses, would he willingly again be used by us?

units.zh: 權柄一去，動轉聽人，魏之宗社，於斯而滅。」
units.en: Once power slips from your hands, you become everyone's puppet—and Wei's altars fall with you."
units.literal: Once power and handle are gone, every move listens to others—Wei's altars and state, at this point are destroyed."

units.zh: 顥由是致疑，稍成疏貳。
units.en: From that Hao grew suspicious and their alliance frayed.
units.literal: From this Hao came to doubt, and gradually estrangement and divided loyalty formed.

units.zh: 慮慶之密啓，乃表高祖曰：「河北、河南一時已定，唯尒朱榮尚敢跋扈，臣與慶之自能擒討。
units.en: Fearing a secret report from Qingzhi, he wrote Emperor Wu: "Hebei and Henan are pacified for now. Only Erzhu Rong still struts defiantly—your servant and Qingzhi can deal with him ourselves.
units.literal: Fearing Qingzhi's secret memorial, he then memorialized the High Ancestor: "Hebei and Henan for the moment are all settled; only Erzhu Rong still dares to be overbearing and unruly—your servant and Qingzhi by ourselves can capture and subdue him.

units.zh: 今州郡新服，正須綏撫，不宜更復加兵，搖動百姓。」
units.en: The provinces have only just submitted and need gentle rule. More troops would only unsettle the people."
units.literal: Now the provinces and commanderies have newly submitted and just need soothing settlement—it is not fitting to add troops again and shake the common people."

units.zh: 高祖遂詔衆軍皆停界首。
units.en: Emperor Wu ordered all reinforcing armies to halt at the frontier.
units.literal: The High Ancestor thereupon ordered all armies to halt at the border passes.

units.zh: 洛下南人不出一萬，羌夷十倍，軍副馬佛念言於慶之曰：「功高不賞，震主身危，二事旣有，將軍豈得無慮？
units.en: Fewer than ten thousand southerners held Luoyang, while Qiang and other tribesmen outnumbered them tenfold. Vice commander Ma Fonian told Qingzhi, "Great merit goes unrewarded, and power that awes one's lord endangers the man who wields it. With both true, can you have no fears?
units.literal: Southerners in Luoyang did not reach ten thousand; Qiang and barbarians were ten times that number. Army Vice Commander Ma Fonian said to Qingzhi: "Merit high but unrewarded, shaking the ruler and peril to the person—these two things are already present; how can the general not have concerns?

units.zh: 自古以來，廢昏立明，扶危定難，鮮有得終。
units.en: Since antiquity, men who deposed bad rulers, raised good ones, and rescued states in peril have rarely died in their beds.
units.literal: From antiquity until now, deposing the dim and establishing the bright, supporting peril and settling difficulty—few have had a good end.

units.zh: 今將軍威震中原，聲動河塞，屠顥據洛，則千載一時也。」
units.en: Your fame now shakes the central plains and the Yellow River frontier. Kill Hao, take Luoyang, and you seize a moment that comes once in a thousand years."
units.literal: Now the general's prestige shakes the central plains and his fame moves the river passes and frontier—slay Hao and hold Luoyang, and it is a once-in-a-thousand-years moment."

units.zh: 慶之不從。
units.en: Qingzhi refused.
units.literal: Qingzhi did not follow.

units.zh: 顥前以慶之爲徐州刺史，因固求之鎮。
units.en: Hao had already named Qingzhi inspector of Xu, and Qingzhi pressed hard to take up that post.
units.literal: Hao had earlier made Qingzhi Inspector of Xu province, and Qingzhi therefore firmly requested to garrison there.

units.zh: 顥心憚之，遂不遣。
units.en: Hao feared to let him go and refused.
units.literal: Hao feared him in his heart and therefore did not send him.

units.zh: 乃曰：「主上以洛陽之地全相任委，忽聞舍此朝寄，欲往彭城，謂君遽取富貴，不爲國計，手敕頻仍，恐成僕責。」
units.en: He said, "The emperor has entrusted all of Luoyang to you. If he hears you mean to abandon that charge for Pengcheng, he will think you grasp at private gain and ignore the realm. His letters come one after another; I fear we will be blamed as servants who failed their master."
units.literal: He then said: "The lord above has wholly entrusted you with the Luoyang region; suddenly I hear you would leave this court commission and wish to go to Pengcheng—he will think you are hastily seizing wealth and rank, not planning for the state; handwritten edicts come repeatedly, and I fear it will become a servant's fault."

units.zh: 慶之不敢復言。
units.en: Qingzhi said no more.
units.literal: Qingzhi did not dare speak again.

units.zh: 魏天柱將軍尒朱榮、右僕射尒朱世隆、大都督元天穆、驃騎將軍尒朱吐沒兒、榮長史高歡、鮮卑、芮芮，勒衆號百萬，挾魏主元子攸來攻顥。
units.en: Wei's Pillar of Heaven Erzhu Rong, Erzhu Shilong, Grand Commander Yuan Tianmu, Erzhu Tumener, Rong's chief clerk Gao Huan, and Xianbei and Rouran allies marched with a host they claimed numbered a million, bringing Emperor Ziyou along to crush Hao.
units.literal: Wei's Pillar of Heaven General Erzhu Rong, Right Vice Director Erzhu Shilong, Grand Commander Yuan Tianmu, Cavalry General Erzhu Tumener, Rong's Chief Clerk Gao Huan, Xianbei, and Rouran led masses they called a million, taking the Wei ruler Yuan Ziyou along to attack Hao.

units.zh: 顥據洛陽六十五日，凡所得城，一時反叛。
units.en: Hao had held Luoyang sixty-five days when every city he had taken rose against him at once.
units.literal: Hao had held Luoyang sixty-five days; all the cities he had gained at once rebelled.

units.zh: 慶之渡河守北中郎城，三日中十有一戰，傷殺甚衆。
units.en: Qingzhi crossed the river and held Beizhonglang fortress. In three days he fought eleven engagements with heavy casualties on both sides.
units.literal: Qingzhi crossed the river and guarded Beizhonglang city; in three days there were eleven battles, and the wounded and slain were very many.

units.zh: 榮將退，時有劉助者，善天文，乃謂榮曰：「不出十日，河南大定。」
units.en: Rong was ready to pull back when Liu Zhu, an expert in astronomy, told him, "Within ten days Henan will be fully pacified."
units.literal: Rong was about to withdraw; at that time there was one Liu Zhu, skilled in astronomy, who said to Rong: "Within no more than ten days Henan will be greatly settled."

units.zh: 榮乃縛木爲筏，濟自硤石，與顥戰於河橋，顥大敗，走至臨潁，遇賊被擒，洛陽陷。
units.en: Rong lashed logs into rafts, crossed at Xiashi, and met Hao at Heqiao. Hao was routed, fled to Linying, was seized by marauders, and Luoyang fell.
units.literal: Rong then bound wood into rafts, crossed from Xiashi, and fought Hao at Heqiao; Hao was greatly defeated, fled to Linying, met bandits and was captured, and Luoyang fell.

units.zh: 慶之馬步數千，結陣東反，榮親自來追，值蒿高山水洪溢，軍人死散。
units.en: Qingzhi withdrew east with a few thousand horse and foot. Erzhu Rong pursued in person. Floods on the Song and Gaoshan ranges drowned and scattered his army.
units.literal: Qingzhi had several thousand horse and foot; he formed battle lines and turned east in retreat. Rong came in person to pursue; they met with floods overflowing the Song Mountains and Gaoshan waters, and soldiers died and scattered.

units.zh: 慶之乃落鬚髮爲沙門，間行至豫州，豫州人程道雍等潛送出汝陰。
units.en: He shaved his beard, took monk's robes, and stole his way to Yu province, where Cheng Daoyong and others smuggled him out through Ruyin.
units.literal: Qingzhi then cut off his beard and hair and became a monk, traveling by secret paths to Yu province; Cheng Daoyong and others of Yu province secretly escorted him out through Ruyin.

units.zh: 至都，仍以功除右衛將軍，封永興縣侯，邑一千五百戶。
units.en: Back in the capital he was made General of the Right Guard for his service and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongxing with a fief of fifteen hundred households.
units.literal: On reaching the capital, he was again appointed by merit as General of the Right Guard and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongxing with a fief of one thousand five hundred households.

units.zh: 出爲持節、都督緣淮諸軍事、奮武將軍、北兗州刺史。
units.en: He was sent out with credentials as commander of Huai frontier forces, General of Stirring Martiality, and inspector of Northern Yan.
units.literal: He went out as bearer of credentials, Commander of all military affairs along the Huai, General of Stirring Martiality, and Inspector of Northern Yan province.

units.zh: 會有妖賊沙門僧強自稱爲帝，土豪蔡伯龍起兵應之。
units.en: A sorcerer-monk named Seng Qiang declared himself emperor, and the local magnate Cai Bolong rose in his support.
units.literal: It happened that the demonic bandit monk Seng Qiang declared himself emperor, and the local strongman Cai Bolong raised troops in response to him.

units.zh: 僧強頗知幻術，更相扇惑，衆至三萬，攻陷北徐州，濟陰太守楊起文棄城走，鐘離太守單希寶見害，使慶之討焉。
units.en: Seng Qiang knew sleight-of-hand and they whipped each other into frenzy until their host reached thirty thousand. They took Northern Xu. Jiyin administrator Yang Qiwen fled; Zhongli administrator Shan Xibao was killed. Qingzhi was ordered to suppress them.
units.literal: Seng Qiang was quite skilled in illusion arts and they fanned and deluded one another; the masses reached thirty thousand, attacked and took Northern Xu province, Administrator of Jiyin Yang Qiwen abandoned the city and fled, Administrator of Zhongli Shan Xibao was killed—the court sent Qingzhi to subdue them.

units.zh: 車駕幸白下，臨餞謂慶之曰：「江、淮兵勁，其鋒難當，卿可以策制之，不宜決戰。」
units.en: The emperor went to Baixia and, at the farewell feast, told Qingzhi, "Jiang and Huai fighters are fierce and hard to meet head-on. Use strategy, not a pitched battle."
units.literal: The imperial carriage went to Baixia; at the farewell feast he said to Qingzhi: "Jiang and Huai troops are strong; their edge is hard to meet—you may use stratagem to control them; it is not fitting to decide the matter in pitched battle."

units.zh: 慶之受命而行。
units.en: Qingzhi took his orders and marched.
units.literal: Qingzhi received the command and set out.

units.zh: 曾未浹辰，斬伯龍、僧強，傳其首。
units.en: Within ten days he had beheaded Bolong and Seng Qiang and sent their heads to court.
units.literal: Before a full ten days had passed, he beheaded Bolong and Seng Qiang and sent their heads.

units.zh: 中大通二年，除都督南北司西豫豫四州諸軍事、南北司二州刺史，餘並如故。
units.en: In the second year of Zhongdatong he was made commander of the four provinces of Southern and Northern Si, Western Yu, and Yu, and inspector of Southern and Northern Si; his other posts remained unchanged.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhongdatong he was appointed Commander of military affairs for the four provinces of Southern and Northern Si, Western Yu, and Yu, and Inspector of the two provinces of Southern and Northern Si; the rest remained as before.

units.zh: 慶之至鎮，遂圍懸瓠。
units.en: On reaching his post Qingzhi at once besieged Xuanhu.
units.literal: When Qingzhi reached his commandery, he thereupon besieged Xuanhu.

units.zh: 破魏潁州刺史婁起、揚州刺史是云寶於溱水，又破行臺孫騰、大都督侯進、豫州刺史堯雄、梁州刺史司馬恭於楚城。
units.en: He routed Wei Inspector of Ying Province Lou Qi and Inspector of Yang Province Shiyun Bao on the Qin River, then defeated mobile headquarters commander Sun Teng, Grand Commander Hou Jin, Inspector of Yu Province Yao Xiong, and Inspector of Liang Province Sima Gong at Chucheng.
units.literal: He defeated Wei Inspector of Ying province Lou Qi and Inspector of Yang province Shiyun Bao at the Qin River, and again defeated Mobile Headquarters Sun Teng, Grand Commander Hou Jin, Inspector of Yu province Yao Xiong, and Inspector of Liang province Sima Gong at Chucheng.

units.zh: 罷義陽鎮兵，停水陸轉運，江湖諸州並得休息。
units.en: He stood down the Yiyang garrison, halted supply convoys by land and water, and gave the river provinces a respite.
units.literal: He dismissed the garrison troops of Yiyang, halted water and land transport of supplies, and the provinces of the rivers and lakes all obtained rest.

units.zh: 開田六千頃，二年之後，倉廩充實。
units.en: He opened six thousand qing of farmland; within two years the granaries were full.
units.literal: He opened six thousand qing of fields; after two years the granaries were full and solid.

units.zh: 高祖每嘉勞之。
units.en: Emperor Wu repeatedly praised and rewarded him.
units.literal: The High Ancestor often praised and comforted him.

units.zh: 又表省南司州，復安陸郡，置上明郡。
units.en: He also memorialized to abolish Southern Si province, restore Anlu commandery, and create Shangming commandery.
units.literal: He also memorialized to abolish Southern Si province, restore Anlu commandery, and establish Shangming commandery.

units.zh: 大同二年，魏遣將侯景率衆七萬寇楚州，刺史桓和陷沒，景仍進軍淮上，貽慶之書使降。
units.en: In the second year of Datong, Wei sent Hou Jing with seventy thousand men against Chu. Inspector Huan He was overrun. Jing pushed on to the Huai and wrote Qingzhi urging surrender.
units.literal: In the second year of Datong, Wei sent the general Hou Jing with seventy thousand men to raid Chu province; Inspector Huan He was lost, and Jing still advanced his army on the Huai and sent Qingzhi a letter urging him to surrender.

units.zh: 敕遣湘潭侯退、右衛夏侯夔等赴援，軍至黎漿，慶之已擊破景。
units.en: The court sent Marquis Tui of Xiangtan, Xiahou Kui of the Right Guard, and others to reinforce him, but by the time they reached Lijiang Qingzhi had already beaten Jing.
units.literal: An edict sent Marquis Tui of Xiangtan, Xiahou Kui of the Right Guard, and others to relieve them; when the army reached Lijiang, Qingzhi had already routed Jing.

units.zh: 時大寒雪，景棄輜重走，慶之收之以歸。
units.en: In bitter cold and snow Jing abandoned his baggage train and fled. Qingzhi gathered the spoils and returned.
units.literal: At that time there was great cold and snow; Jing abandoned his baggage train and fled, and Qingzhi gathered it and returned.

units.zh: 進號仁威將軍。
units.en: He was promoted to General of Humane Prestige.
units.literal: His title was advanced to General of Humane Prestige.

units.zh: 是歲，豫州饑，慶之開倉賑給，多所全濟。
units.en: That year Yu province suffered famine. Qingzhi opened the granaries and saved many lives.
units.literal: That year Yu province suffered famine; Qingzhi opened the granaries for relief and distribution, and many were wholly saved.

units.zh: 州民李升等八百人表請樹碑頌德，詔許焉。
units.en: Eight hundred residents led by Li Sheng petitioned for a stele in his honor, and the court approved.
units.literal: Eight hundred common people of the province, Li Sheng and others, submitted a memorial requesting a stele to praise his virtue, and an edict permitted it.

units.zh: 五年十月，卒，時年五十六。
units.en: In the tenth month of the fifth year he died, aged fifty-six.
units.literal: In the tenth month of the fifth year he died, at the age of fifty-six.

units.zh: 贈散騎常侍、左衛將軍，鼓吹一部。
units.en: He was posthumously made attendant cavalier at large and general of the left guard, with a full military band for his funeral.
units.literal: Posthumously he was given Attendant Cavalier at Large and General of the Left Guard, and one set of martial music.

units.zh: 諡曰武。
units.en: His posthumous title was Martial.
units.literal: His posthumous name was Martial.

units.zh: 敕義興郡發五百丁會喪。
units.en: The court ordered Yixing commandery to send five hundred laborers for the funeral.
units.literal: An edict ordered Yixing commandery to dispatch five hundred corvée laborers to attend the funeral.

units.zh: 慶之性祗慎，衣不紈綺，不好絲竹，射不穿札，馬非所便，而善撫軍士，能得其死力。
units.en: Qingzhi was sober and modest: no fine silks, no music, no skill at archery or horsemanship—yet he knew how to win soldiers' hearts and draw their utmost loyalty.
units.literal: Qingzhi's nature was respectful and cautious; he did not wear silk damask, did not love string and bamboo music, in archery could not pierce a leaf, and horse riding was not his forte—yet he was good at soothing soldiers and could obtain their strength unto death.

units.zh: 長子昭嗣。
units.en: His eldest son was Zhaosi.
units.literal: His eldest son was Zhaosi.

units.zh: 第五子昕，字君章。
units.en: His fifth son was Xin, styled Junzhang.
units.literal: His fifth son was Xin, styled Junzhang.

units.zh: 七歲能騎射。
units.en: At seven he could ride and shoot.
units.literal: At seven he could ride and shoot.

units.zh: 十二隨父入洛，於路遇疾，還京師。
units.en: At twelve he followed his father to Luoyang, fell ill on the road, and returned to the capital.
units.literal: At twelve he followed his father into Luoyang; on the road he fell ill and returned to the capital.

units.zh: 詣鴻臚卿朱异，异訪北間形勢，昕聚土畫地，指麾分別，异甚奇之。
units.en: He visited Grand Herald Zhu Yi, who asked about conditions in the north. Xin piled earth to sketch a map and traced out the terrain with his finger. Yi was astonished.
units.literal: He called on Grand Herald Zhu Yi; Yi inquired about conditions in the north, and Xin piled earth to draw the land, directing and distinguishing with his hand—Yi greatly marveled at him.

units.zh: 大同四年，爲邵陵王常侍、文德主帥、右衛仗主，敕遣助防義陽。
units.en: In the fourth year of Datong he served Prince Shaoling as attendant, commander of the Civil Virtue corps, and master of arms of the Right Guard, and was ordered to help defend Yiyang.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Datong he was Attendant to the Prince of Shaoling, Commander of Civil Virtue, and Master of Arms of the Right Guard; an edict sent him to assist in defending Yiyang.

units.zh: 魏豫州刺史堯雄，北間驍將，兄子寶樂，特爲敢勇。
units.en: Wei Yu inspector Yao Xiong was a famed northern fighter; his nephew Baole was exceptionally daring.
units.literal: Yao Xiong, Inspector of Yu province under Wei, was a fierce general of the north; his elder brother's son Baole was especially bold and brave.

units.zh: 慶之圍懸瓠，雄來赴其難，寶樂求單騎校戰，昕躍馬直趣寶樂，雄卽散潰，仍陷溱城。
units.en: While Qingzhi besieged Xuanhu, Xiong marched to relieve it. Baole asked for single combat. Xin spurred straight at him; Xiong's force broke and fled, and they took Qincheng.
units.literal: Qingzhi besieged Xuanhu; Xiong came to relieve the crisis; Baole requested single-horse trial combat; Xin leaped on his horse and charged straight at Baole; Xiong at once scattered in rout, and they still took Qincheng.

units.zh: 六年，除威遠將軍、小峴城主，以公事免。
units.en: In the sixth year he was made General of Awesome Distance and lord of Xiaoxian, then dismissed for an official offense.
units.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed General of Awesome Distance and lord of Xiaoxian city, but was dismissed on account of public business.

units.zh: 十年，妖賊王勤宗起於巴山郡，以昕爲宣猛將軍，假節討焉。
units.en: In the tenth year the rebel Wang Qinzong rose in Bashan commandery. Xin was named General of Manifest Valor with acting credentials to suppress him.
units.literal: In the tenth year the demonic bandit Wang Qinzong rose in Bashan commandery; Xin was made General of Manifest Valor with acting credentials to subdue him.

units.zh: 勤宗平，除陰陵戍主、北譙太守，以疾不之官。
units.en: After Qinzong was crushed he was named garrison commander of Yinling and administrator of Northern Qiao, but illness kept him from taking office.
units.literal: When Qinzong was pacified, he was appointed garrison commander of Yinling and Administrator of Northern Qiao, but because of illness did not take office.

units.zh: 又除驃騎外兵，俄爲臨川太守。
units.en: He was then made outer troops officer under the cavalry general and soon administrator of Linchuan.
units.literal: He was again appointed Outer Troops of the Cavalry General, and shortly became Administrator of Linchuan.

units.zh: 太清二年，侯景圍歷陽，敕召昕還，昕啓云：「採石急須重鎮，王質水軍輕弱，恐慮不濟。」
units.en: In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing besieged Liyang. The court recalled Xin, but he reported, "Caishi needs a strong garrison at once. Wang Zhi's fleet is too light—I fear it will fail."
units.literal: In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing besieged Liyang; an edict recalled Xin; Xin reported: "Caishi urgently needs a heavy garrison; Wang Zhi's water army is light and weak—I fear it will not succeed."

units.zh: 乃板昕爲雲騎將軍，代質，未及下渚，景已渡江，仍遣率所領遊防城外，不得入守。
units.en: He was hastily named General of Cloud Cavalry to replace Zhi. Before Xin reached Xiazhu, Jing had crossed the Yangzi. Xin was posted outside the walls on patrol and could not enter to defend.
units.literal: He was then appointed on the board as General of Cloud Cavalry to replace Zhi; before reaching Xiazhu, Jing had already crossed the Yangzi, and Xin was still sent to lead his command in roaming defense outside the walls, unable to enter and hold the defense.

units.zh: 欲奔京口，乃爲景所擒。
units.en: He tried to flee to Jingkou but was seized by Jing.
units.literal: He wished to flee to Jingkou but was captured by Jing.

units.zh: 景見昕殷勤，因留極飲，曰：「我至此得卿，餘人無能爲也。」
units.en: Jing found Xin obliging and kept him for a long drinking bout, saying, "With you in hand I need no one else."
units.literal: Jing saw that Xin was attentive and courteous and therefore detained him for extreme drinking, saying: "In coming here I have obtained you; the rest are incapable of acting."

units.zh: 令昕收集部曲，將用之，昕誓而不許。
units.en: He ordered Xin to rally his troops for service. Xin swore he would not comply.
units.literal: He ordered Xin to gather his troops and intended to use him; Xin swore an oath and would not consent.

units.zh: 景使其儀同范桃棒嚴禁之，昕因說桃棒令率所領歸降，襲殺王偉、宋子仙爲信。
units.en: Jing had his officer Fan Taobang guard him closely. Xin persuaded Taobang to lead his men in surrender and kill Wang Wei and Song Zixian as proof of good faith.
units.literal: Jing had his Protocol Equal Fan Taobang strictly confine him; Xin thereupon persuaded Taobang to lead those under his command to return and surrender, and to attack and kill Wang Wei and Song Zixian as proof of good faith.

units.zh: 桃棒許之，遂盟約，射啓城中，遣昕夜縋而入。
units.en: Taobang agreed. They sealed a pact, shot a message into the city, and sent Xin in by rope at night.
units.literal: Taobang agreed; they then made a covenant, shot a message into the city, and sent Xin in by night on a rope.

units.zh: 高祖大喜，敕卽受降，太宗遲疑累日不決，外事發洩，昕弗之知，猶依期而下。
units.en: Emperor Wu was delighted and ordered the surrender accepted at once, but the Heir Apparent hesitated for days. The matter leaked. Xin knew nothing and came down on schedule.
units.literal: The High Ancestor was greatly pleased and ordered that the surrender be accepted at once; the Heir Apparent hesitated for many days without deciding; the matter leaked outside; Xin did not know of this and still descended according to schedule.

units.zh: 景邀得之，乃逼昕令更射書城中，云「桃棒且輕將數十人先入。」
units.en: Jing caught him and forced him to shoot another message into the city: "Taobang will send only a few dozen men inside first."
units.literal: Jing intercepted and seized him, then forced Xin to shoot another letter into the city saying "Taobang will first send only a few dozen light troops to enter."

units.zh: 景欲裹甲隨之。
units.en: Jing meant to follow in armor himself.
units.literal: Jing wished to wrap his armor and follow after.

units.zh: 昕旣不肯爲書，期以必死，遂爲景所害，時年三十三。
units.en: Xin refused to write the letter, accepting death, and Jing killed him. He was thirty-three.
units.literal: Xin would not write the letter and expected certain death; he was thereupon killed by Jing, at the age of thirty-three.

units.zh: 蘭欽字休明，中昌魏人也。
units.en: Lan Qin, styled Xiuming, came from Zhongchangwei.
units.literal: Lan Qin, styled Xiuming, was a native of Zhongchangwei.

units.zh: 父子雲，天監中，軍功官至雲麾將軍，冀州刺史。
units.en: His father Ziyun rose through military merit in the Tianjian era to General of the Cloud Pennon and inspector of Ji.
units.literal: His father was Ziyun; in the Tianjian era, through military merit he reached General of the Cloud Pennon and Inspector of Ji province.

units.zh: 欽幼而果決，篸捷過人。
units.en: Qin was resolute from childhood, and his agility surpassed others.
units.literal: Qin was resolute from childhood, and his agility surpassed others.

units.zh: 隨父北征，授東宮直閤。
units.en: He accompanied his father on the northern campaign and was appointed Direct Guard of the Eastern Palace.
units.literal: He accompanied his father on the northern campaign and was appointed Direct Guard of the Eastern Palace.

units.zh: 大通元年，攻魏蕭城，拔之。
units.en: In Datong 1, he attacked Wei's Xiao city and took it.
units.literal: In Datong 1, he attacked Wei's Xiao city and took it.

units.zh: 仍破彭城別將郊仲，進攻擬山城，破其大都督劉屬衆二十萬。
units.en: He then defeated Jiao Zhong, a detached general from Pengcheng, advanced to attack Nishan city, and defeated the two hundred thousand troops of its grand commander Liu Shu.
units.literal: He then defeated Jiao Zhong, a detached general from Pengcheng, advanced to attack Nishan city, and defeated the two hundred thousand troops of its grand commander Liu Shu.

units.zh: 進攻籠城，獲馬千餘匹。
units.en: He advanced to attack Longcheng and captured more than one thousand horses.
units.literal: He advanced to attack Longcheng and captured more than one thousand horses.

units.zh: 又破其大將柴集及襄城太守高宣、別將范思念、鄭承宗等。
units.en: He also defeated their great general Chai Ji, Gao Xuan, administrator of Xiangcheng, and the detached generals Fan Sinian, Zheng Chengzong, and others.
units.literal: He also defeated their great general Chai Ji, Gao Xuan, administrator of Xiangcheng, and the detached generals Fan Sinian, Zheng Chengzong, and others.

units.zh: 仍攻厥固、張龍、子城，未拔，魏彭城守將楊目遣子孝邕率輕兵來援，欽逆擊走之。
units.en: He then attacked Juegu, Zhanglong, and Zicheng, but had not yet taken them when Yang Mu, Wei's defending general at Pengcheng, sent his son Xiaoyong with light troops to reinforce them; Qin met him and drove him off.
units.literal: He then attacked Juegu, Zhanglong, and Zicheng, but had not yet taken them when Yang Mu, Wei's defending general at Pengcheng, sent his son Xiaoyong with light troops to reinforce them; Qin met him and drove him off.

units.zh: 又破譙州刺史劉海游，還拔厥固，收其家口。
units.en: He also defeated Liu Haiyou, Wei's inspector of Qiaozhou, returned to take Juegu, and seized his household.
units.literal: He also defeated Liu Haiyou, Wei's inspector of Qiaozhou, returned to take Juegu, and seized his household.

units.zh: 楊目又遣都督范思念、別將曹龍牙數萬衆來援，欽與戰，于陣斬龍牙，傳首京師。
units.en: Yang Mu again sent commander Fan Sinian and detached general Cao Longya with tens of thousands to reinforce the city. Qin fought them, beheaded Longya in battle, and sent his head to the capital.
units.literal: Yang Mu again sent commander Fan Sinian and detached general Cao Longya with tens of thousands to reinforce the city. Qin fought them, beheaded Longya in battle, and sent his head to the capital.

units.zh: 又假欽節，都督衡州三郡兵，討桂陽、陽山、始興叛蠻，至卽平破之。
units.en: He was again given acting credentials and command of Heng province's three commanderies to suppress rebellious tribes in Guiyang, Yangshan, and Shixing. He crushed them on arrival.
units.literal: He was again given acting credentials and made Commander of the three commandery armies of Heng province to subdue the rebellious Man of Guiyang, Yangshan, and Shixing; on arrival he at once pacified and broke them.

units.zh: 封安懷縣男，邑五百戶。
units.en: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Anhuai with a fief of five hundred households.
units.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Anhuai county with a fief of five hundred households.

units.zh: 又破天漆蠻帥晚時得。
units.en: He also defeated the Tianqi tribal chief Wanshide.
units.literal: He again defeated the Tianqi Man chieftain Wanshide.

units.zh: 會衡州刺史元慶和爲桂陽人嚴容所圍，遣使告急，欽往應援，破容羅溪，於是長樂諸洞一時平蕩。
units.en: Heng inspector Yuan Qinghe was besieged by Yan Rong of Guiyang and sent for help. Qin marched to relieve him, routed Rong at Luoxi, and pacified the Changle hill country in one sweep.
units.literal: It happened that Yuan Qinghe, Inspector of Heng province, was besieged by Yan Rong of Guiyang; he sent envoys in urgent appeal; Qin went to relieve him, defeated Rong at Luoxi, and thereupon all the caves of Changle were pacified at one stroke.

units.zh: 又密敕欽向魏興，經南鄭，屬魏將托跋勝寇襄陽，仍敕赴援。
units.en: A secret order sent him toward Weixing by way of Nanzheng. When Wei general Tuoba Sheng raided Xiangyang he was ordered to reinforce.
units.literal: There was also a secret edict ordering Qin toward Weixing, passing Nanzheng; it happened that the Wei general Tuoba Sheng raided Xiangyang, and he was again ordered to go to relieve.

units.zh: 除持節、督南梁、南、北秦、沙四州諸軍事、光烈將軍、平西校尉、梁南秦二州刺史，增封五百戶，進爵爲侯。
units.en: He received credentials as commander of Southern Liang, Southern Qin, Northern Qin, and Sha, was named General of Bright Valor and Colonel Who Pacifies the West, and inspector of Liang and Southern Qin. His fief grew by five hundred households and he was raised to marquis.
units.literal: He was appointed bearer of credentials, Commander of military affairs for the four provinces of Southern Liang, Southern Qin, Northern Qin, and Sha, General of Bright Valor, Colonel Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of the two provinces of Liang and Southern Qin; his fief was increased by five hundred households and his rank advanced to Marquis.

units.zh: 破通生，擒行臺元子禮、大將薛俊、張菩薩，魏梁州刺史元羅遂降，梁、漢底定。
units.en: He defeated Tongsheng and captured mobile headquarters commander Yuan Zili and the generals Xue Jun and Zhang Pusa. Yuan Luo, the Wei Inspector of Liang Province, then surrendered, and the Liang and Han regions were secured.
units.literal: He defeated Tongsheng, captured Mobile Headquarters Yuan Zili, Grand Generals Xue Jun and Zhang Pusa; Yuan Luo, Inspector of Liang province under Wei, thereupon surrendered, and Liang and Han were settled at the root.

units.zh: 進號智武將軍，增封二千戶。
units.en: He was promoted to General of Sagacious Martiality with two thousand additional households in his fief.
units.literal: His title was advanced to General of Sagacious Martiality and his fief increased by two thousand households.

units.zh: 俄改授持節、都督衡、桂二州諸軍事、衡州刺史。
units.en: He was soon reassigned with credentials as commander of Heng and Gui and inspector of Heng.
units.literal: Shortly he was reassigned as bearer of credentials, Commander of military affairs for the two provinces of Heng and Gui, and Inspector of Heng province.

units.zh: 未及述職，魏遣都督董紹、張獻攻圍南鄭，梁州刺史杜懷瑤請救。
units.en: Before he took up his post, Wei commanders Dong Shao and Zhang Xian besieged Nanzheng. Liang inspector Du Huaiyao called for aid.
units.literal: Before he had reported to his post, Wei sent Commanders Dong Shao and Zhang Xian to attack and besiege Nanzheng; Du Huaiyao, Inspector of Liang province, requested relief.

units.zh: 欽率所領援之，大破紹、獻于高橋城，斬首三千餘，紹、獻奔退，追入斜穀，斬獲略盡。
units.en: Qin marched to relieve them and routed Shao and Xian at Gaoqiao, taking more than three thousand heads. They fled; he pursued into Xie Pass and killed or captured nearly all of them.
units.literal: Qin led those under his command to relieve them and greatly defeated Shao and Xian at Gaoqiao city, beheading more than three thousand; Shao and Xian fled in rout; he pursued into Xiegu and those slain and captured were nearly all.

units.zh: 西魏相宇文黑泰致馬二千匹，請結鄰好。
units.en: Western Wei chancellor Yuwen Heitai sent two thousand horses and asked for friendly relations.
units.literal: The Chancellor of Western Wei, Yuwen Heitai, sent two thousand horses and requested to form neighborly good relations.

units.zh: 詔加散騎常侍，進號仁威將軍，增封五百戶，仍令述職。
units.en: The court added attendant cavalier at large, promoted him to General of Humane Prestige, increased his fief by five hundred households, and ordered him to take up his post.
units.literal: An edict added Attendant Cavalier at Large, advanced his title to General of Humane Prestige, increased his fief by five hundred households, and still ordered him to report to his post.

units.zh: 經廣州，因破俚帥陳文徹兄弟，並擒之。
units.en: Passing through Guang province he defeated the Li chieftains Chen Wenche and his brothers and took them captive.
units.literal: Passing through Guang province, he thereupon defeated the Li chieftains Chen Wenche and his brothers and captured them all.

units.zh: 至衡州，進號平南將軍，改封曲江縣公，增邑五百戶。
units.en: At Heng province he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the South, made Duke of Qujiang, and given five hundred more households.
units.literal: On reaching Heng province his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the South, he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Qujiang county, and his fief increased by five hundred households.

units.zh: 在州有惠政，吏民詣闕請立碑頌德，詔許焉。
units.en: His rule in the province was benevolent. Officials and people petitioned the court for a commemorative stele, and the edict approved.
units.literal: While in the province he had benevolent government; officials and common people went to the court to request a stele praising his virtue, and an edict permitted it.

units.zh: 徵爲散騎常侍、左衛將軍，尋改授散騎常侍、安南將軍、廣州刺史。
units.en: He was recalled as attendant cavalier at large and general of the left guard, then reassigned as attendant cavalier, general who pacifies the south, and inspector of Guang.
units.literal: He was summoned as Attendant Cavalier at Large and General of the Left Guard; shortly he was reassigned as Attendant Cavalier at Large, General Who Pacifies the South, and Inspector of Guang province.

units.zh: 旣至任所，前刺史南安侯密遣廚人置藥於食，欽中毒而卒，時年四十二。
units.en: On reaching his post, the former inspector, Marquis of Nan'an, secretly had his cook poison Qin's food. Qin died, aged forty-two.
units.literal: Once he had reached his place of duty, the former Inspector, the Marquis of Nan'an, secretly sent his kitchen man to place poison in the food; Qin was poisoned and died, at the age of forty-two.

units.zh: 詔贈侍中、中衛將軍，鼓吹一部。
units.en: He was posthumously made palace attendant and general of the central guard, with a military band for his funeral.
units.literal: An edict posthumously gave him Palace Attendant and General of the Central Guard, and one set of martial music.

units.zh: 子夏禮，侯景至歷陽，率其部曲邀擊景，兵敗死之。
units.en: His son Xiali, when Hou Jing reached Liyang, led his troops to ambush Jing, was defeated, and died.
units.literal: His son Xiali—when Hou Jing reached Liyang, he led his troops to intercept and strike Jing, was defeated in battle, and died.

units.zh: 史臣曰：陳慶之、蘭欽俱有將略，戰勝攻取，蓋頗、牧、衛、霍之亞歟。
units.en: The historiographer writes: Chen Qingzhi and Lan Qin both possessed true generalship. In victory and conquest they stand in the company of Lian Po, Li Mu, Wei Qing, and Huo Qubing.
units.literal: The historiographer says: Chen Qingzhi and Lan Qin both had military strategy; victorious in battle and taking by assault—they were perhaps the peers of Lian Po, Li Mu, Wei Qing, and Huo Qubing.

units.zh: 慶之警悟，早侍高祖，旣預舊恩，加之謹肅，蟬冕組珮，亦一世之榮矣。
units.en: Qingzhi was quick-witted and attended Emperor Wu from youth. Old favor, sober conduct, and the regalia of high office were glory enough for one life.
units.literal: Qingzhi was alert and perceptive; he early attended the High Ancestor, and having shared in old favor, together with his respectful sobriety, cicada cap and ribbon pendant—these too were the glory of a lifetime.

units.zh: 王羆 子慶遠 孫述 王思政
units.en: Wang Pi — Qingyuan — Shu — Wang Sizheng
units.literal: Wang Pi; his son Qingyuan; his grandson Shu; Wang Sizheng

units.zh: 王羆字熊羆，京兆霸城人，漢河南尹王遵之後，世為州郡著姓。
units.en: Wang Pi, styled Xiongpi, came from Bachecheng in Jingzhao commandery. He descended from Wang Zun, governor of Henan under the Han, and his family had long been a leading name in the provinces.
units.literal: Wang Pi, styled Xiongpi, was a native of Bachecheng in Jingzhao commandery, a descendant of Wang Zun, governor of Henan under Han, for generations a prominent surname in the provinces and commanderies.

units.zh: 進封霸城縣公。
units.en: He was promoted to Duke of Bachecheng.
units.literal: His rank was advanced to Duke of Bachecheng county.

units.zh: 年八歲，太祖見而奇之，曰：「王公有此孫，足為不朽。」
units.en: When he was eight, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai met him, was impressed, and said: "Duke Wang has a grandson like this; his name will endure."
units.literal: At age eight, the Grand Progenitor saw him and thought him remarkable, saying: "Duke Wang has this grandson—enough to be immortal."

units.zh: 魏太和中，除殿中將軍。
units.en: During the Taihe era of Emperor Xiaowen of Wei he was made palace-guard general.
units.literal: In Wei Emperor Xiaowen's Taihe era, he was appointed palace-guard general.

units.zh: 以羆為荊州刺史，進號撫軍將軍。
units.en: Wang Pi was appointed governor of Jing Province and promoted to general who pacifies the army.
units.literal: Pi was made governor of Jing Province; his title was advanced to general who pacifies the army.

units.zh: 子慶遠，弱冠以功臣子拜直閤將軍。
units.en: His son Qingyuan, still in his teens and as the son of a meritorious minister, was made direct-pavilion general.
units.literal: His son Qingyuan, at weak-crown age as a meritorious minister's son was appointed direct-pavilion general.

units.zh: 大統七年，卒於鎮，贈太尉。
units.en: In Datong 7 (541) he died at his post and was posthumously made grand commandant.
units.literal: In the seventh year of Datong, he died at his garrison post; posthumously given grand commandant.

units.zh: 先是南岐、東益氐羌反叛，王師戰不利，乃令羆領羽林五千鎮梁州，討平諸賊。
units.en: When Di and Qiang rebels rose in Southern Qi and East Yizhou and the imperial army faltered, Wang Pi was sent with five thousand Yulin guards to garrison Liang Province and put down the uprisings.
units.literal: Previously Southern Qi and East Yizhou Di and Qiang had rebelled; the imperial army fought unfavorably; he was then ordered to lead five thousand Yulin guards to garrison Liang Province and pacify the various rebels.

units.zh: 還，授右將軍、西河內史。
units.en: On his return he was given the posts of right general and interior minister of West He commandery.
units.literal: Returning, he was granted right general and interior minister of West He.

units.zh: 辭不拜。
units.en: He refused the appointment.
units.literal: He declined and did not accept the appointment.

units.zh: 羆曰：「京洛材木，盡出西河，朝貴營第宅者，皆有求假。
units.en: Wang Pi answered: "All the timber for Luoyang comes from West He, and every court noble building a mansion comes asking to borrow it.
units.literal: Pi said: "Timber for the capital at Luoyang all comes from West He; court nobles building mansions all have requests to borrow.

units.zh: 如其私辦，卽力所不堪，若科發民間，又違法憲。
units.en: If I pay for it myself, I cannot afford it; if I levy it from the people, I break the law.
units.literal: If by my own means I supply it, I immediately cannot bear the burden; if I levy it from the common people, I again violate law and charter.

units.zh: 以此辭耳。」
units.en: That is why I declined."
units.literal: For this reason I decline—that is all."

units.zh: 每出戰，嘗不擐甲冑，大呼曰：「荊州城，孝文皇帝所置。
units.en: Whenever he fought he often went without armor and cried out: "This city of Jing Province was founded by Emperor Xiaowen.
units.literal: Each time he went out to battle he usually did not don armor; he shouted loudly: "Jing Province city was established by Emperor Xiaowen.

units.zh: 天若不佑國家，使賊箭中王羆；
units.en: If Heaven will not save the realm, let the enemy's arrows find Wang Pi;
units.literal: If Heaven does not protect the state, let the rebels' arrows strike Wang Pi;

units.zh: 不爾，王羆須破賊。」
units.en: If not, Wang Pi will break the enemy."
units.literal: If not, Wang Pi must break the rebels."

units.zh: 羆不應命，謂其使曰：「若茹茹至渭北者，王羆率鄉里自破之，不煩國家兵馬。
units.en: Wang Pi ignored the summons and told the messenger: "If the Rouran reach the north bank of the Wei, Wang Pi will rally the local people and break them himself. There is no need to trouble the imperial army.
units.literal: Pi did not respond to the summons; he told the envoy: "If the Rouran reach north of the Wei River, Wang Pi will lead the village folk to break them himself—no need to trouble the state's troops and horses.

units.zh: 何為天子城中，遂作如此驚動。
units.en: Why turn the Son of Heaven's own city into such a panic?
units.literal: Why in the Son of Heaven's city make such alarm and commotion?

units.zh: 由周家小兒恇怯致此。」
units.en: This uproar comes from that coward Zhou boy."
units.literal: It is because the Zhou family's young fellow is cowardly that this has come about."

units.zh: 羆曰：「耕種收穫，其功已深；
units.en: Wang Pi said: "From plowing and sowing through the harvest, the labor is long;
units.literal: Pi said: "In plowing and sowing, harvesting—the labor is already deep;

units.zh: 舂爨造成，用力不少。
units.en: and from threshing and cooking to the finished cake, the work is great.
units.literal: Pounding and cooking to make it—the effort is not small.

units.zh: 乃爾選擇，當是未饑。」
units.en: If you can pick and choose like that, you cannot be hungry yet."
units.literal: Yet you choose like this—you cannot yet be hungry."

units.zh: 梁將曹義宗圍荊州，勑羆與別將裴衍率兵赴救。
units.en: When Liang general Cao Yizong besieged Jing Province, an edict sent Wang Pi with separate commander Pei Yan to relieve the city.
units.literal: Liang general Cao Yizong besieged Jing Province; an edict ordered Pi together with separate commander Pei Yan to lead troops to the rescue.

units.zh: 遂與梁人戰，大破之。
units.en: They met the Liang army and routed it.
units.literal: Thereupon they fought the Liang men and greatly defeated them.

units.zh: 梁復遣曹義宗衆數萬圍荊州，堰水灌城，不沒者數板。
units.en: Liang sent Cao Yizong back with tens of thousands of men, dammed the river, and flooded the city until only a few courses of wall stood above the water.
units.literal: Liang again sent Cao Yizong with a host of tens of thousands to besiege Jing Province; they dammed the water to flood the city, and only several boards of wall remained unsubmerged.

units.zh: 時旣內外多虞，未遑救援，乃遺羆鐵券，云城全當授本州刺史。
units.en: With crises on every front the court could spare no relief force, but it sent Wang Pi an iron certificate promising him the governorship if he kept the city intact.
units.literal: At that time both within and without there were many worries; there was no leisure to send relief; they therefore sent Pi an iron certificate, saying if the city remained whole he would be granted governor of that province.

units.zh: 城中糧盡，羆煮粥，與將士均分而食之。
units.en: When food ran out inside the walls, Wang Pi cooked gruel and shared it equally with his officers and soldiers.
units.literal: Inside the city grain was exhausted; Pi cooked gruel and divided it equally with officers and soldiers to eat.

units.zh: 屢經戰陣，亦不被傷。
units.en: He fought again and again and was never hurt.
units.literal: He repeatedly passed through battle formations and was also not wounded.

units.zh: 彌歷三年，義宗方退。
units.en: Three years passed before Cao Yizong finally withdrew.
units.literal: More than three years passed before Yizong finally withdrew.

units.zh: 尋遷車騎大將軍、涇州刺史。
units.en: He was soon made grand general of chariots and cavalry and governor of Jingzhou (Jing Prefecture).
units.literal: Soon he was transferred to grand general of chariots and cavalry and governor of Jing Province.

units.zh: 未及之部，屬太祖徵兵為勤王之舉，請前驅效命，遂為大都督，鎮華州。
units.en: Before he took office, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai mobilized for the rescue of the emperor; Wang Pi volunteered for the vanguard, was made grand commander, and garrisoned Huazhou.
units.literal: Before he reached his post, it happened that the Grand Progenitor raised troops for the campaign to rescue the ruler; he requested to serve as vanguard and give his life; he thereupon became grand commander and garrisoned Huazhou.

units.zh: 魏孝武西遷，拜驃騎大將軍，加侍中、開府。
units.en: When Emperor Xiaowu fled west, Wang Pi received the rank of grand general of fast cavalry, with palace attendant and opening-the-feudatory as well.
units.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Pi was appointed grand general of fast cavalry, with additional posts as palace attendant and opening-the-feudatory.

units.zh: 齊神武遣韓軌、司馬子如從河東宵濟襲羆，羆不之覺。
units.en: Gao Huan sent Han Gui and Sima Ziru to cross the Yellow River from Hedong by night and strike Wang Pi, who did not detect them.
units.literal: Gao Huan sent Han Gui and Sima Ziru to cross the Yellow River by night from Hedong and raid Pi; Pi did not notice.

units.zh: 比曉，軌衆已乘梯入城。
units.en: By dawn Han Gui's men were already climbing the ladders into the city.
units.literal: By dawn, Gui's troops had already mounted the ladders and entered the city.

units.zh: 羆尚臥未起，聞合外洶洶有聲，便袒身露髻徒跣，持一白挺，大呼而出。
units.en: Wang Pi was still in bed when he heard uproar at the gate. He threw off his clothes, let down his hair, went barefoot, seized a white club, and charged out shouting.
units.literal: Pi was still lying down and had not risen; hearing a clamorous noise outside the inner gate, he bared his torso, loosened his hair, went barefoot, grasped a white club, and shouted as he came out.

units.zh: 敵見之驚，逐至東門，左右稍集，合戰破之。
units.en: The enemy fell back in shock. He drove them to the east gate, his men rallied around him, and together they broke the attack.
units.literal: The enemy seeing him were startled; he drove them to the east gate; his attendants gradually gathered; they joined battle and defeated them.

units.zh: 軌衆遂投城遁走。
units.en: Han Gui's force then jumped from the walls and fled.
units.literal: Gui's troops thereupon leapt from the walls and fled.

units.zh: 時關中大饑，徵稅民間穀食，以供軍費。
units.en: Guanzhong was in famine, and grain was requisitioned from the people to feed the army.
units.literal: At that time Guanzhong suffered great famine; grain was levied from among the people to supply military expenses.

units.zh: 或隱匿者，令遞相告，多被篣棰，以是人有逃散。
units.en: Anyone hiding grain was to be reported by his neighbors; many were flogged with bamboo, and people fled in fear.
units.literal: Those who concealed grain were ordered to inform on one another; many were beaten with bamboo rods, and thereby people fled and scattered.

units.zh: 唯羆信著于人，莫有隱者，得粟不少諸州，而無怨讟。
units.en: Only in Wang Pi's jurisdiction did people trust him enough to surrender their grain willingly. He collected no less than other provinces, and no one complained.
units.literal: Only Pi's trustworthiness was renowned among the people; there were none who concealed; the grain obtained was not less than other provinces, yet without complaints and slander.

units.zh: 沙苑之役，齊神武士馬甚盛。
units.en: At the Battle of Shaye, Gao Huan's army was overwhelming.
units.literal: At the Battle of Shaye, Gao Huan's troops and horses were very strong.

units.zh: 太祖以華州沖要，遣使勞羆，令加守備。
units.en: Because Huazhou was a vital point, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai sent an envoy to encourage Wang Pi and told him to strengthen the defenses.
units.literal: The Grand Progenitor because Huazhou was strategically critical sent an envoy to encourage Pi and ordered him to increase defensive preparations.

units.zh: 羆語使人曰：「老羆當道臥，貆子安得過！」
units.en: Wang Pi told the messenger: "Old Pi lies across the road. What badger cub thinks he can slip by?"
units.literal: Pi told the envoy: "Old Pi lies across the road—how can a badger cub get past!"

units.zh: 太祖聞而壯之。
units.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai admired his boldness when he heard this.
units.literal: The Grand Progenitor hearing it admired his spirit.

units.zh: 及齊神武至城下，謂羆曰：「何不早降？」
units.en: When Gao Huan came beneath the walls he called to Wang Pi: "Why not surrender now?"
units.literal: When Gao Huan reached beneath the walls, he said to Pi: "Why not surrender early?"

units.zh: 羆乃大呼曰：「此城是王羆冢，生死在此，欲死者來。」
units.en: Wang Pi shouted back: "This city is Wang Pi's tomb. Life and death are here. Whoever wants to die, come!"
units.literal: Pi thereupon shouted loudly: "This city is Wang Pi's tomb; life and death are here—whoever wishes to die, come."

units.zh: 齊神武遂不敢攻。
units.en: Gao Huan did not dare press the assault.
units.literal: Gao Huan thereupon did not dare attack.

units.zh: 左僕射周惠達召羆議之。
units.en: Left vice director Zhou Huida summoned Wang Pi to consult him.
units.literal: Left vice director Zhou Huida summoned Pi to discuss it.

units.zh: 未幾，還鎮河東。
units.en: Before long he returned to garrison Hedong.
units.literal: Before long, he returned to garrison Hedong.

units.zh: 羆輕侮權勢，守正不回，皆此類也。
units.en: Wang Pi scorned power, held to principle, and never bent—this was typical of him.
units.literal: Pi slighted authority and power, held to the upright and did not bend—all were of this kind.

units.zh: 羆性儉率，不事邊幅。
units.en: Wang Pi was plain and frugal by nature and cared nothing for appearances.
units.literal: Pi by nature was frugal and plain; he did not attend to niceties of appearance.

units.zh: 史臣曰：王羆剛峭有餘，弘雅未足。
units.en: The historiographer writes: Wang Pi was more than stern enough, but lacked refined magnanimity.
units.literal: The historiographer says: Wang Pi had stern sharpness in surplus, but magnanimous elegance was not enough.

units.zh: 情安儉率，志在公平。
units.en: He was content with plain living and set his heart on fairness.
units.literal: His disposition rested content in thrift and plainness; his will was set on fairness.

units.zh: 旣而奮節危城，抗辭勍敵，梁人為之退舍，高氏不敢加兵。
units.en: Yet he upheld his integrity in a doomed city and defied fierce foes with bold words, so the Liang forces withdrew before him and the Gao clan did not dare attack.
units.literal: Thereafter he exerted integrity in a perilous city and matched words with fierce enemies; Liang men withdrew on his account, and the Gao clan did not dare bring troops.

units.zh: 以此見稱，信非虛。
units.en: His reputation was well deserved.
units.literal: To be famed for this was truly not empty.

units.zh: 嘗有臺使，羆為其設食。
units.en: Once when an imperial envoy came, Wang Pi served him a meal.
units.literal: Once there was an imperial envoy; Pi set out food for him.

units.zh: 使乃裂其薄餅緣。
units.en: The envoy tore away the crust of his flatbread.
units.literal: The envoy then tore off the rim of his thin cake.

units.zh: 命左右撤去之。
units.en: He had his attendants take the food away.
units.literal: He ordered his attendants to remove it.

units.zh: 使者愕然大慙。
units.en: The envoy was stunned and deeply ashamed.
units.literal: The envoy was startled and greatly ashamed.

units.zh: 又有客與羆食瓜，客削瓜侵膚稍厚，羆意嫌之。
units.en: Another time a guest shared melon with Wang Pi and cut away rather too much flesh, which Wang Pi quietly resented.
units.literal: There was also a guest dining with Pi on melon; the guest pared the melon, cutting the flesh rather thick; Pi inwardly disliked it.

units.zh: 及瓜皮落地，乃引手就地，取而食之。
units.en: When the rind fell to the floor, he reached down, picked it up, and ate it.
units.literal: When the melon rind fell to the ground, he reached his hand to the ground, picked it up, and ate it.

units.zh: 客甚有愧色。
units.en: The guest flushed with shame.
units.literal: The guest was deeply ashamed.

units.zh: 性又嚴急，嘗有吏挾私陳事者，羆不暇命捶扑，乃手自取鞾履，持以擊之。
units.en: He was harsh as well. Once when a clerk came with a private petition, Wang Pi did not bother to order a beating; he pulled off his boot and struck the man with it.
units.literal: His nature was also strict and sharp; once when a clerk brought a private matter for judgment, Pi had no leisure to order flogging; he himself took off boot and shoe and struck him with them.

units.zh: 羆剛直木強，處物平當，州郡敬憚之。
units.en: Wang Pi was blunt, stubborn, and scrupulously fair, and officials across the provinces both admired and feared him.
units.literal: Pi was upright, stubborn, and unyielding; in dealing with things he was fair and even; the provinces and commanderies respected and feared him.

units.zh: 先羆卒，孫述嗣。
units.en: Qingyuan died before Wang Pi, and the grandson Shu inherited the line.
units.literal: Qingyuan died before Pi; his grandson Shu succeeded.

units.zh: 述幼喪父，為羆所鞠養。
units.en: Shu had lost his father young and was raised by Wang Pi.
units.literal: Shu from youth lost his father; he was reared and nurtured by Pi.

units.zh: 魏行台崔孝芬、大都督刁宣馳往圍暄，晝夜急攻，戊寅，暄突走，擒斬之。
units.en: The Wei mobile-staff director Cui Xiaofen and grand commander Diao Xuan raced to besiege Xuan, attacking day and night; on wuyin, Xuan broke out, fled, and was captured and executed.
units.literal: The Wei mobile-staff Director Cui Xiaofen and Grand Commander Diao Xuan galloped to invest Xuan, attacking day and night; on day wuyin, Xuan broke out and fled and was captured and killed.

units.zh: 元天穆與驃騎將軍爾朱吐沒兒將大軍前後繼至，梁士卒皆恐。
units.en: Yuan Tianmu and the General of Agile Cavalry, Erzhu Tumener, brought up great armies one after another, and the Liang troops were seized with fear.
units.literal: Yuan Tianmu and the General of Agile Cavalry Erzhu Tumener led great armies arriving in succession, and the Liang soldiers were all afraid.

units.zh: 俄而天穆等引兵圍城，慶之帥騎三千背城力戰，大破之，天穆、吐沒兒皆走。
units.en: Soon Tianmu and the others invested the city; Qingzhi led three thousand horsemen in a fight with their backs to the wall and smashed them; Tianmu and Tumener both fled.
units.literal: Soon Tianmu and the others brought troops to encircle the city; Qingzhi led three thousand horsemen to fight with their backs to the wall and routed them; Tianmu and Tumener both fled.

units.zh: 孝昌元年，北邊擾亂，奔雲中，為刺史費穆送於尒朱榮。
units.en: In the first year of Xiaochang, when the northern frontier fell into disorder, he fled to Yunzhong and was sent by Inspector Fei Mu to Erzhu Rong.
units.literal: In the first year of Xiaochang, when the northern frontier fell into disorder, he fled to Yunzhong and was sent by Inspector Fei Mu to Erzhu Rong.

units.zh: 高祖撥亂反正，深鑒奢逸，惡衣菲食，務先節儉。
units.en: Gaozu ended chaos and restored rule, deeply wary of extravagance, preferring coarse dress and plain fare and putting thrift first.
units.literal: Emperor Gaozu quelled disorder and restored order, taking deep warning from luxury and excess, wearing poor clothes and eating plain food, putting frugality first.

units.zh: 后，宋元嘉中嬪於文帝，生長沙宣武王懿、永陽昭王敷，次生高祖。
units.en: In Song's Yuanjia era she entered Emperor Wen's harem and bore Yi, Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, Fu, Prince Zhao of Yongyang, and later Gaozu.
units.literal: In Yuanjia of Song she became a consort to Emperor Wen and bore Yi, Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, Fu, Prince Zhao of Yongyang, and afterward bore Gaozu.

units.zh: 是月產高祖。
units.en: That month she gave birth to Gaozu.
units.literal: That month she gave birth to Gaozu.

units.zh: 高祖踐阼，追贈穆之光祿大夫，加金章。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Muzhi was posthumously made Glory Grand Master with a gold seal.
units.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Muzhi was posthumously made Glory Grand Master with gold seal.

units.zh: 高祖郗皇后
units.en: Empress Xi of Gaozu
